title: Add checkpointed streaming RAG quickstart with resumable incremental outputs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Teams building long-running RAG features (large context, streaming generation, and background index updates) need an opinionated example showing how to stream partial generations while persisting lightweight checkpoints so a session can resume after a crash or deploy. This quickstart demonstrates a small, production-oriented pattern: (1) incremental streaming of model output, (2) periodic checkpointing of the agent session state (prefix/KV cache pointers + retrieval cursor), and (3) a resumable client/server flow that can pick up where it left off. The goals are: reproducible dev experience, minimal infra (local file or Redis examples), and observability probes for partial-output coverage.

What this PR adds (single continuous description): - A new quickstart folder examples/streaming-checkpoint with two language bindings: a TypeScript example (app.ts + README) and a Go server example (server.go) demonstrating streaming HTTP endpoints. - A new docs page docs/streaming-checkpoint.md that explains the pattern, failure modes, checkpoint schema, and recommended SLOs for checkpoint intervals. - A quickstart manifest quickstart.yaml that can be used with the local dev runner (devcontainer/local-run) to bring up the example and a Redis instance for checkpoint persistence. - Telemetry probe presets telemetry/probes.json for measuring partial-output frequency, checkpoint latency, and resume success rate. - CI workflow update ci/workflows/quickstarts.yml to run smoke tests for the new example on node/go matrix.

High level changes touched: README.md (index linking the quickstart), examples/streaming-checkpoint/README.md (how to run locally), examples/streaming-checkpoint/app.ts (ts example of client-side checkpointing and streaming reconnection logic), examples/streaming-checkpoint/server.go (go server demonstrating incremental checkpoint writes and safe KV cache invalidation), docs/streaming-checkpoint.md (conceptual guide), quickstart.yaml (start instructions), telemetry/probes.json (probe definitions), ci/workflows/quickstarts.yml (add matrix entry and smoke test steps).

Example usage: 1) Start the quickstart: ./dev/run-quickstart quickstart.yaml --name streaming-checkpoint 2) From the TS client: yarn && yarn dev:start which will open a streaming WebSocket to the server and periodically write checkpoints to Redis at configurable intervals. 3) Simulate a crash, restart the client; the client queries the checkpoint endpoint /v1/checkpoint?session_id=... and the server will return the last known token index + retrieval cursor so streaming resumes without redoing expensive retrieval or repeating tokens.

Checkpoint schema (short): {session_id, last_emitted_token_index, retrieval_cursor_id, kv_cache_pointer, model_variant, epoch_iso}. The server stores a compressed JSON blob and exposes a small /v1/checkpoint GET/POST API. Checkpoints are intentionally minimal to be safe for fast writes and to limit KVS cost.

Telemetry: probes included measure (a) checkpoint_write_latency_ms, (b) checkpoint_size_bytes, (c) resume_success_fraction, (d) partial_output_events_per_session. The docs explain recommended alert thresholds (e.g., resume_success_fraction < 0.95 triggers an SRE runbook link).

Developer notes and motivation details: - We avoid full KV-cache serialization; instead we rely on a pointer-based checkpoint that references per-node persistent prefix files produced by the runtime. This mirrors how Redwood Dedicated runtime exposes immutable prefix snapshots. - The example demonstrates two persistence backends: local FS (fast dev) and Redis for more realistic deployment testing. - The TS example intentionally includes a small reconciliation loop that reconciles emitted tokens with model state to avoid duplication when resuming streaming. - The Go server includes careful delete-on-rotate semantics for checkpoint TTL to avoid stale resume paths in multi-tenant scenarios.

Security and privacy: Checkpoint blobs are treated as customer-owned data; the quickstart shows how to enable simple encryption-at-rest for local files and a KMS-backed Redis encryption example in docs/notes. The quickstart README reminds users not to store sensitive PII in checkpoints during evaluation runs.

Backward compat: No API breaking changes to runtime. This is an additive example and docs-only in the platform. The telemetry probes are additive and gated behind quickstart config so customers opting into example telemetry are opt-in.

Checklist included in description: - [x] Add TS and Go examples and README - [x] Add conceptual docs page and diagrams - [x] Add quickstart manifest and CI smoke-tests - [x] Add telemetry probes and example dashboards - [x] Add small unit+integration smoke test (node/go) in CI

Related: ENG-1289 (design spike for resumable streaming), PM-347 (customer ask: resumable RAG sessions), and a follow-up item ENG-1427 planned to integrate the checkpointed pattern with Redwood Optimize recommendations.
commit_summary: Initial skeleton of streaming-checkpoint example (TS + Go) and README
Add docs/streaming-checkpoint.md and diagrams explaining checkpoint schema
Implement Redis and FS checkpoint backends with tests
Add telemetry probes and quickstart manifest
CI: add smoke matrix entry for example (node 18 / go 1.20)
review_comments: Priya Singh: Nice pattern — can we add a short section on expected checkpoint frequency trade-offs? (latency vs. lost tokens).
Maya Chen (author): Added a FAQ subsection in docs/streaming-checkpoint.md covering trade-offs and included recommended defaults (500ms or every 8 tokens).
Ethan Morales: Server.go looks solid. Please add a small unit test for checkpoint read failure case to ensure resume returns a coherent error for clients.
Maya Chen (author): Added tests/checkpoint_fail_test.go and updated CI to run it in the go matrix.
Luca Romano: Minor nit — telemetry probe names should follow kebab-case. Updated probes.json accordingly. Approved after CI passes.
release_notes: Add: New quickstart 'checkpointed streaming RAG' that demonstrates resumable streaming sessions with FS/Redis checkpoint backends, telemetry probes, and TS/Go examples. Useful for teams building long-running RAG features that require crash-resume functionality.
notes_for_merger: Squash-merge. Keep PR description as the squash commit message. Tag release-notes with quickstart addition and notify docs channel for site indexing.
manual_steps_documented: Yes - docs/streaming-checkpoint.md contains local dev steps, env var config (REDIS_URL, CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_MS), and instructions for toggling FS vs Redis backends.
